stories.headline: Penix's return revives Falcons' attack in rout of Packers
stories.summary: In his first game since tearing his ACL last November, Michael Penix Jr. sparked the Falcons by passing for 256 yards with a touchdown in a 35-14 rout of the Packers at Lambeau Field.
stories.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Michael Penix Jr. cried in the locker room before the Atlanta Falcons' last preseason game in August, according to Falcons safety Jessie Bates III. Penix was emotional because he knew he was not ready to return from left ACL surgery last November.

On Thursday, Penix finally came back and helped lead the Falcons to a stunning 35-14 rout of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. In his first game since tearing his ACL in Week 11 last November, Penix was 18-of-25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

Bates said Penix was "dying to get back."

"I know how much it means to him," Bates said. "I know how much he means to the locker room."

Penix threw an interception on the first series but then settled down. By the second quarter, he was cruising. During the second and third quarters, Penix was 13-of-15 passing with a touchdown and 5-of-5 on third downs. The score came on a 5-yard pass to tight end Austin Hooper with 59 seconds left in the first half.

"Definitely after that interception, I started getting a rhythm, and everything started clicking," Penix said.

As it has been in his first two seasons, Penix's favorite target was wide receiver Drake London, who had nine catches for a career-high 194 yards.

"He's the definition of resiliency," London said of Penix.

The Falcons (1-2) struggled during the first two weeks of the season. With Penix not yet ready, Tua Tagovailoa was tabbed as the Week 1 starter. But Tagovailoa injured his oblique three days before the first game of the season and had to be spelled by third-string quarterback Cooper Rush.

Rush was also dealing with back spasms, and the Falcons' offense was nonexistent. They scored a combined 16 points over two games, the lowest mark in the league. Atlanta did not take a red zone snap, a skid that was finally broken after 27 straight series to begin the season, tied for the second-longest such streak in the past 45 seasons.

With Penix back under center, the Falcons' hope -- and firepower -- seemed restored. Running back Bijan Robinson had 194 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said he felt great for Penix and lauded the hard work he put in to return to the field.

"It's not easy to rehab from injuries," Stefanski said. "That's a tough thing to do when he's putting himself through the extra workouts in the weight room, the extra treatments in the training room. All those times that he's out on the field running and no one was watching. It's just him and the trainers and the medical staff. So proud of all of that. I got to witness it, and this, tonight, is something you can build on."

But the Falcons won't rest on their laurels, either.

"We got a long season to go," Penix said. "That game was far from perfect, and that's what we're striving for each and every day. So, obviously we're going to go back and look at the film, find things that we can do better."

stories.headline: Top-seeded Lynx heavy favorites for WNBA title entering playoffs
stories.summary: The Lynx will head into the 2026 WNBA playoffs as the favorites to win the title, followed by the Aces and Valkyries.
stories.body:
The Minnesota Lynx will head into the 2026 WNBA playoffs as the favorites to win the title -- one of several surprises from before the season, according to the odds.

Minnesota tops the WNBA Finals odds board at +115, a distinct improvement from the fifth-best +800 odds the Lynx had coming into the 2026 campaign. The Las Vegas Aces are next at +475, followed by the Golden State Valkyries at +550 -- another surprise, given that the 2025 expansion team entered its second season of play with long 45-1 odds to win the championship, according to DraftKings lines.

A pair of ankle injuries to franchise player Napheesa Collier kept the Lynx from being a preseason favorite despite their contending pedigree, but what pushed them into stand-alone favorite status was the emergence of likely Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles, forcing bookmakers to move the lines when Minnesota started hot and never looked back.

"They showed early on how good they were, and then it was like, 'OK, well, they're this good and they're getting Collier back,'" Caesars Sportsbook pro basketball lead David Lieberman told ESPN. "The market, we all adjusted down on them pretty quickly compared to what they were preseason."

The Lynx were actually bigger favorites earlier in the final weeks of the regular season, reaching odds-on status, but lengthened to their current level once the playoff picture was solidified Thursday night.

Their title pursuit will begin with a series against the New York Liberty, who began the season favored to win the title at +220 but are now a much longer 14-1, per DraftKings odds. Bookmakers say there hasn't been a lot of action this season on the disappointing squad, but they are paying attention to the team's championship potential.

"At 14-1, there's not a lot of interest," DraftKings Sportsbook director Johnny Avello told ESPN. "In Round 1, I wouldn't count any of these teams out. I mean, you could see upsets, I don't think there's going to be any big surprise if they do happen. And the Liberty, they've won it before. They know how to win, they know what playing in the playoffs is all about."

The Liberty are +280 in their series with the Lynx, who are -350.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the biggest liability across the sportsbook marketplace is the Indiana Fever, who go into the postseason with +950 odds to win it all. Given the immense popularity of the squad -- to the tune of 25% of the handle at DraftKings -- and the relatively long odds they had at times this season, the caution adds up quickly for sportsbooks.

"The Fever, I feel like as long as Caitlin Clark is there, are probably always going to be our liability, our worst-case scenario for the championship futures," Lieberman said. "So they are No. 1 by a decent chunk."

BetMGM trading manager Seamus Magee echoed the sentiment, noting Indiana is the most-bet team for the title by wagers and handle at the sportsbook. Bookmakers across the marketplace also say there is some liability on the very popular Paige Bueckers-led Dallas Wings, but they are less worried about that given that Dallas is the longest team on the board at 80-1, per DraftKings lines.

The Fever are +155 underdogs to win their series against the Aces at -185, while the Wings are an even longer +330 to the Valkyries' -425 for the series.

The liability on the longer teams means that sportsbooks are in decent shape at the top: "The Lynx and Aces, the betting favorites, are good outcomes for the sportsbook," Magee said over email.

Sportsbooks also have released odds for Finals MVP, with Minnesota's Collier and Miles leading the way at +280 and +320, respectively, per DraftKings lines. A'ja Wilson (+600), Gabby Williams (12-1) and Clark (15-1) round out the top five.

stories.body:
Major League Baseball implemented the ABS challenge system for the 2026 season, which allows players to challenge a ball or strike call made by the plate umpire. Each team receives two challenges to start the game, and only batters, pitchers and catchers can challenge a call. If a team wins a challenge, it can keep challenging. If a team challenges incorrectly twice, it loses its challenges for the rest of the game.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Anthony Gordon: Premier League players most fatigued at summer tournaments
stories.summary: Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.
stories.body:
Anthony Gordon has said Premier League players are destined to come into summer tournaments more fatigued than any other league.

The inquest into England's painful World Cup semifinal defeat to Argentina continues, with focus on their energy-sapping style of football and inability to keep the ball in the same way that Spain can.

Boss Tuchel said fatigue played a part in their capitulation, coming on the back of extra time in their quarterfinal win against Norway in Miami heat and emotionally-draining victories against Congo DR and Mexico.

Gordon says those playing in the relentlessness of the Premier League are at a disadvantage at the back end of tournaments.

"I think that would probably be a fact," he said. "I don't know the stats, but I think for sure because in England, I'm not saying there is an easy game in any other leagues, but every game is as hard as the next.

"Playing Arsenal is the same as playing a newly-promoted side. That's the difficulty of the Premier League. Every game is so intense. Anyone can win a game.

"I mean, I think Hull, a newly-promoted team, were unbeaten until they played Newcastle.

"So that shows the strength of the Premier League, the strength of the English game, and I think for the English players playing in the Premier League, it would be a lot tougher on the body than players elsewhere."

Gordon's substitution in the semifinal remains a big talking point -- he was withdrawn 16 minutes after putting his side 1-0 up and replaced by a defender.

- Tuchel's England dilemma: Emulate Spain or embrace Premier League 'chaos'?

- Bukayo Saka: 'Tough' to stay on England bench in Argentina World Cup loss

- Harry Kane: Argentina defeat was most painful England moment yet

The game quickly unravelled after that and Gordon said that match needed a lot of unpacking in his personal diary afterwards.

"It was more than one page, I can tell you that," he added. "Maybe not consistently, but I always like to write things down. It just makes you feel more clear.

"I think everyone does that in a different way. Some people use laptops, or some people don't like to do anything.

"My version of that has always been just to write it down, and I kind of like it because I can look back on it and pass it on to my kids.

"But the Argentina game was probably the most memorable one I've had because I didn't really know what to write. I wrote down just pure emotion of what I felt.

"Obviously, I won't go into those details, but it was it was a good few pages, I can tell you."

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Merab Dvalishvili; 4. Ilia Topuria; 5. Alexander Volkanovski; 6. Joshua Van; 7. Arman Tsarukyan; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Makhachev; 2. Volkanovski; 3. Gaethje; 4. Topuria; 5. Pereira; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Van; 8. Gane; 9. Yan; 10. Tsarukyan.

Andrew Davis: 1. Makhachev; 2. Tom Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Topuria; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Tsarukyan.

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Gaethje; 6. Volkanovski; 7. Topuria; 8. Van; 9. Gane; 10. Pereira.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Van; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Tsarukyan; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Volkanovski.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail preliminary finals: McLean explains long-term Panthers deal
stories.summary: Isaah Yeo and Moses Leota are both keens to remain Panthers despite interest elsewhere, while Casey McLean is happy for his departing brother.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's preliminary finals weekend.

McLean reveals why he committed long-term to Panthers

Casey McLean has opened up on his decision to commit his long-term future to Penrith, describing his extension through the end of 2030 as another "pinch-me" moment in his rapid rise.

Having grown up in the area and played his junior football with the Panthers, McLean said remaining at the club was an opportunity to repay the faith Penrith showed by handing him his first-grade opportunity.

"Obviously this club, playing for them, growing up my whole life around this area... being able to give back to them, I suppose," McLean said.

"They want me around, but being able to think that I played my juniors here and they want me to stay, that's kind of my way of giving back.

"The coaches and the staff, they gave me my first opportunity to show myself on the big stage, and I think it's just kind of a way I can give back to them as well."

McLean is contracted to Penrith until the end of 2030, positioning the young centre as a key piece of the club's next generation.

McLean opens up on replacing Crichton

Casey McLean has revealed the message from Penrith that helped ease the pressure of stepping into the centre position vacated by Stephen Crichton last year.

McLean admitted he initially arrived in first grade feeling as though he had to replace the premiership-winning centre, before being encouraged to forge his own identity.

"I walked in here thinking... I've got to replace Critta," McLean said.

"But coming here, the boys and coach, they're kind of just like, 'There's no shoes to fill. You've got to take the spot and make it your own, kind of play to your strengths.'

"'You wouldn't be here for no reason. You've worked hard... just be yourself.'"

McLean has since established himself as a key member of Penrith's backline as the Panthers continue transitioning into their next generation.

Leota disappointed to miss Warriors showdown

Moses Leota has admitted there was some disappointment in seeing the Warriors' season come to an end, denying Penrith a potential finals meeting with his former front-row partner James Fisher-Harris.

Leota retains strong ties to New Zealand and spent years forming one of the NRL's premier prop combinations alongside Fisher-Harris at Penrith before the Kiwi international's move across the Tasman.

"They had a really great season," Leota said of the Warriors.

"It's very sad, but it is what it is. There's some weapons in that team, right? They'll get back here next year."

McLean relishing Gagai battle

Casey McLean is preparing for another battle with veteran Knights centre Dane Gagai, declaring the 35-year-old is still performing as though he is in his prime.

McLean has previously spent time around Gagai in representative camp and has also faced the Queensland veteran on several occasions at NRL level.

"He's such an amazing guy," McLean said.

"I don't think he lets his age [affect him]... he still looks like he's in his prime.

"He's still running around, he's still doing what he's doing, leaving his mark on the game.

Yeo and Leota's future

Isaah Yeo has confirmed his preference is to remain at Penrith beyond his current contract, and is hoping to sort out his future following the end of the season.

"It always has been [my preference to stay]," Yeo admitted.

"The idea is to stay at Penrith as a one club player."

Moses Leota has also affirmed his love for Penrith, with the hope a deal gets done following the 2026 finals.

"[Remaining at Penrith] is massive to me," he shared.

"I've been here basically my whole life."

Casey McLean backs brother at Bulldogs

Panthers gun Casey McLean admitted while he's "gutted" that his brother Jesse will be leaving Penrith next year, but he's excited to see him flourish at Canterbury.

"Obviously pretty gutted that we won't be on the same team," he told ESPN.

"It'll be a weird feeling at first, but I'm super excited for the opportunity that he'll be given [at the Bulldogs]."

He went on to vouch for Jesse's ability on the field, expecting his older brother to remind fans of his talent.

"He does talk a little s--- on the field," Casey joked.

"But he's just an amazing player - he helped me grow as well.

"He's such an amazing role model, not only for myself, but for a fair few boys here as well."

stories.headline: Caitlin Clark: Fever focused on playoffs after blowout loss to Lynx
stories.summary: Indiana is the No. 6 seed in the playoffs for the third consecutive season after losing 86-66 to Minnesota on Thursday.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Forty-eight hours after the Indiana Fever cruised past the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx for one of their best wins of the season, the Fever had one of their worst defeats in one of their most consequential games of the season.

In the regular-season finale, Indiana suffered an 86-66 loss to the Lynx in a game that wasn't as close as the final score indicated. The Fever trailed by 30 points at halftime and 36 in the third quarter before head coach Stephanie White pulled her starters. Four-time All-Star Aliyah Boston aggravated a lower leg injury and didn't return, and reserve Tyasha Harris had to be carried off the court because of a left ankle injury.

The Fever fell to the No. 6 seed for the third consecutive season and will be on the road to open the playoffs against the No. 3-seeded Las Vegas Aces on Sunday. Indiana lost two of three to end the regular season, including a 93-77 defeat to the Mystics, after winning eight of 10.

The Lynx will host the New York Liberty in a rematch of the 2024 WNBA Finals on Sunday.

White said after the game that Boston experienced a flare-up in her knee and didn't play in the second half for precautionary reasons. White called Harris' injury an awkward fall but didn't have an update on her status.

Caitlin Clark was held to a career-low two points on 1-for-12 shooting. Kelsey Mitchell's league record of 27 consecutive games with at least 20 points ended as she finished with 10 points on 3-for-12 shooting.

"At this point, everybody's record is 0-0," Clark said. "We're going into the playoffs. If we sit and sulk about what happened tonight, yeah, it sucks. It is what it is. We kind of came out and got punched in the mouth. We didn't make shots, obviously.

"I'm excited. If you can't get up for the playoffs, then you probably shouldn't be on this team. That's the great thing. You look at one through eight in this league right now, [and] it's anybody's to take. We have to have the mentality going into the playoffs of let's go steal the first one."

Though the Fever were talking about moving on from a disappointing effort, the Lynx had already done so. Coach Cheryl Reeve benched her starters Tuesday when the Lynx trailed by 23 points at halftime against the Fever.

The lack of energy and execution that plagued the team in Indianapolis was gone Thursday, as the Lynx jumped out to a 25-4 lead and never looked back. Kayla McBride, who was held scoreless Tuesday, hit six 3-pointers and finished with a game-high 22 points. Natasha Howard added 21.

"I was just really proud of how we bounced back," McBride said. "Like, it's not easy. Social media, we see everything. Everything that you guys post, Twitter, blah blah blah. I turned it off because everybody's talking about we're 1-4 in the last game[s] and da da da da. We got benched. All this stuff. It's like noise.

"And it's everybody, and it's natural, right? But there's nothing anybody can do or say when we're between those four lines. And I felt like we just came out and we did that."

The Fever went 2-1 against the Aces during the regular season and will travel from Minneapolis to Las Vegas. Though Clark was excited about the playoffs, the team hoped for a higher seed during the season and had spoken about the importance of home-court advantage after losing Game 5 on the road to the Aces in the semifinals last season.

Defense continues to be Indiana's biggest weakness. The Fever are 11th in points allowed per game but have the No. 1 offense in the league.

"This is playoff basketball," White said. "The physicality, the intensity level, the level of focus. ... I don't believe we shoot like that very often. We just have to not let that affect us on the other end. ... It's 0-0, and we're still playing basketball, and so we flush this one. We learn from it, we grow from it, and we start our prep for whoever we're playing tomorrow."

stories.headline: Flyers' Zegras gets penalty for tucking jersey into pants
stories.summary: Flyers forward Trevor Zegras was given a minor penalty for "improperly wearing the equipment" in Thursday's preseason game after being warned about tucking his jersey into his pants.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Flyers forward Trevor Zegras was given a minor penalty for "improperly wearing the equipment" in a preseason game Thursday night after being warned about tucking his jersey into his pants.

The penalty was issued in the second period of the Flyers' 2-0 home win over the Boston Bruins.

"My jersey was tucked in at the start of my shift. So after a warning, they said that's an automatic penalty," Zegras said. "I started the game with it tucked, which is obviously how I usually play."

Scouting The Refs, a website that tracks NHL officiating, reported that Zegras was the first player to be penalized for a jersey tuck violation since 2013.

Rule 9.5 states that "all protective equipment, except gloves, headgear, neck protection, and goalkeepers' leg pads must be worn under the uniform." Under Rule 12.1, which covers all illegal equipment, players are given a warning before a minor penalty is imposed.

Flyers coach Rick Tocchet said teams were told a few weeks ago that proper use of equipment would be an officiating emphasis this season.

"He's just gotta put his tie down. That'll keep the jersey down," Tocchet said after the game, referencing the loop of fabric that secures a jersey to a player's pants. "He obviously can't [tuck] it anymore. When the regular season starts, we can't have a penalty like that."

The last time the NHL cracked down on tucked-in jerseys was in 2013-14. The enforcement was unpopular with some players, with Washington Capitals star Alex Ovechkin calling it "kind of stupid" and saying that it restricted the individuality of the players.

stories.headline: Padres beat Dodgers 4-2 to clinch a franchise-record 3rd straight postseason berth
stories.summary: — Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ethan Salas had RBI singles in a three-run seventh inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 4-2 on Thursday night to clinch their franchise-record third consecutive postseason berth and fifth in seven seasons.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ethan Salas had RBI singles in a three-run seventh inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 4-2 on Thursday night to clinch their franchise-record third consecutive postseason berth and fifth in seven seasons.


It didn't come easily.


The Dodgers closed to 4-2 in the ninth on Shohei Ohtani's RBI double off Padres closer Mason Miller.


Yuki Matsui (1-1) got the victory in relief. Miller earned his 38th save.


Dodgers starter Tyler Glasnow (5-2) struck out a season-high 11 and took a no-hitter into the sixth, when Salas and Tatis broke it up with back-to-back singles. Salas scored on Dustin Harris' sacrifice fly to center.


The Padres got Glasnow out of the game in the seventh after Jackson Merrill doubled and Xander Bogaerts walked. Merrill scored from second as pinch-hitter Austin Hays' single against reliever Justin Wrobleski went off third baseman Max Muncy's glove.


Salas' two-strike single to center scored Bogaerts. Tatis followed with an RBI single for a 4-0 lead.


It was Glasnow's second straight game with at least 10 strikeouts. He gave up three runs and three hits.


While the Padres clinched a berth, the Dodgers locked up a bye and the Milwaukee Brewers secured home field advantage throughout the playoffs.


They avoided the wild-card round and earned home-field advantage in the NL Division Series before stepping on the field after Cincinnati beat Atlanta 7-6. The two-time defending World Series champions will open the postseason on Oct. 3.


The Dodgers' other run was scored on a balk by Adrian Morejon in the eighth.


Ohtani was back in the Dodgers' leadoff spot since the Padres started a right-handed pitcher. He was 2 for 5 with a strikeout. He batted second behind Mookie Betts and also went 1 for 4 in his return from the injured list on Wednesday.


Padres starter Nick Pivetta struck out five of nine batters in his first trip through the Dodgers' lineup. He gave up back-to-back, two-out hits to Ohtani and Betts before Freddie Freeman took a called third strike to end the inning.


Up next 
Padres: They had yet to announce a starter for Friday's series opener against D-backs RHP Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.72 ERA).


Dodgers: LHP Tarik Skubal (11-7, 2.85) starts Friday at San Francisco against Giants RHP Yunior Marte (0-1, 4.66).

stories.headline: Freo coach wants to emulate Lions' sustained success
stories.summary: Whether Fremantle win or lose the AFL grand final, coach and former Dockers player Justin Longmuir wants the game to be the start of an era of success.
stories.body:
Even the always-measured Justin Longmuir concedes he has dreamt of what it would be like to take Fremantle to an elusive first premiership.

But the Fremantle coach cares more about making sure the AFL's perennial underdogs reach grand-final week every year, like Chris Fagan's two-time reigning premiers Brisbane, rather than one moment in the sun.

Longmuir, the former Fremantle ruckman, can earn Dockers immortality in Saturday's Grand Final against the Lions at the MCG and said it was "hard not to" think about doing so.

"I've thought about this moment for a number of years," Longmuir said.

"And I think when I first went into coaching, I always had the goal in the back of my mind to lead us to this position and it would fill me with great pride to be able to do that.

"But win or lose tomorrow, it's not the end of the journey.

"As a football club, we want to create something that 'Fages' has created, where you're contending for a number of years. So whether we win tomorrow, it's not full stop on the journey or what we set out to achieve.

"It's another moment, big moment, and something that will fill us with enormous pride and our fans will be able to celebrate, but it's not the end of the journey.

"We've got a lot of work ahead of us to be able to create a team and a club that competes year in year out like these guys (Brisbane) are."

Skipper Alex Pearce is also hungrily eyeing off the prospect of leading the Dockers to the holy grail.

"(It's) definitely something that I have been conscious of," Pearce said.

"But I think as it's gotten closer to the game, I've been really mindful of controlling what we can control.

"And I've made sure that my efforts and attention and the team's efforts and attention are going into things that matter and that can help us win on on game day - and wanting to win really bad isn't gonna help us."

Brisbane veteran Lachie Neale is the only current player left from the Fremantle team that lost the 2013 Grand Final to Hawthorn - the Dockers' one previous Grand Final.

Shai Bolton (Richmond), Luke Jackson (Melbourne) and Mason Cox (Collingwood) are Fremantle's premiership winners at their previous clubs.

Longmuir was adamant the minor premiers are prepared.

"This hasn't been a flash in the pan. It hasn't been 'oh, we've gone on a good streak and landed in the Grand Final'," he said.

"We've built over a number of years for this moment. We played the type of footy that we feel holds up at this time of the year."

stories.headline: Pelinka: Lakers grateful for run with LeBron, exit 'done amicably'
stories.summary: Rob Pelinka said Thursday that the Lakers remain thankful for their time with LeBron James.
stories.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- Los Angeles Lakers president of basketball operations and general manager Rob Pelinka said LeBron James' decision to leave the franchise this summer was "done amicably" and that the Lakers remain thankful for their time with the all-time great.

"I thought it would be appropriate at the front to express gratitude for the LeBron era here," Pelinka said Thursday before a season-opening news conference alongside Lakers coach JJ Redick.

"Clearly, new team and new players, and that's what we're going to talk about today. But we as an organization are still grateful for the run that we had with him here."

Thursday's news conference was two months to the day since James agreed to a two-year, $8 million deal with the Philadelphia 76ers and an occasion for Pelinka to share his first remarks about James' departure.

"The Lakers have become -- as they should -- a perennial playoff team," Pelinka continued, looking back at James' eight years in L.A. "Won a championship, went to the Western Conference finals. It was a great era, and we're grateful for it. I think it's important to say that at the onset as we turn into a new chapter."

James' longtime friend and agent, Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, informed the Lakers about eight hours before the official start of free agency on June 30 that his client would be seeking a new team.

The decision was an about-face from James' previous public stance during NBA All-Star weekend in Indianapolis in February 2024.

"I am a Laker and I'm happy and been very happy being a Laker the last six years and hopefully it stays that way," James said at the time.

James' choice also came after Pelinka publicly lobbied to bring James back during an exit interview news conference with reporters in May following the Lakers' second-round exit against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

"LeBron, we probably haven't seen a player that has honored the game to the extent that he's honored the game," Pelinka said May 12. "He's given so much to his teammates, to this organization. And the thing we want to do more than anything else is honor him back. ... Any team, including ours, would love to have LeBron James on their roster."

Pelinka was asked, considering those statements from James and the Lakers in the past, why he thinks the 41-year-old star is now in Philadelphia.

"Again, we're grateful for the LeBron era," Pelinka said. "I think the communications with him this offseason were held diplomatically, professionally and honestly. I'm so thankful for the partnership that we had that continued up until this summer when a decision was made for him to play for another team. It was done amicably, professionally, gracefully. We looked at the whole thing with gratitude, because it's been an incredible era for us here."

Redick, James' former "Mind the Game" podcast co-host before stepping onto the Lakers' sidelines, did not specifically address the four-time champion's departure. Redick already showed public support for James, however, shortly after James informed L.A. he would be leaving by showing up to James' live taping of "Mind the Game" with Tyrese Haliburton at Fanatics Fest in New York in July.

Redick did endorse L.A.'s roster construction once James left, though.

"I think with this group, probably the first time in my three years here that I feel like the pieces actually fit together," Redick said.

Other than a series of tweets thanking the Lakers after announcing the Sixers as his fourth -- and final -- team he will play for before retirement, James has yet to elaborate on his L.A. exit.

Fans will not have to wait much longer to hear James' side of things. A new episode of "Mind the Game" is scheduled to be released Friday. In an Instagram post teasing the release, James' co-host, Steve Nash, asks him, "How did you come to Philly? What led to saying, like, 'That's my destination'?"

James also will address reporters for the first time since his decision when the Sixers hold their annual media day Monday in Camden, New Jersey.

stories.headline: Former England forward Andy Carroll says he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021
stories.summary: Former England forward Andy Carroll has revealed in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.
stories.body:
Former England forward Andy Carroll has said in his autobiography he was sexually assaulted by a man during 2021.

The 37-year-old included the details in his book, titled "Owning It." As a victim of sexual assault, Carroll was automatically granted anonymity.

Carroll said the incident took place at his home during a second spell at Newcastle. The offender -- a friend of his former partner, who was staying away at the time -- was later jailed for three years, with Carroll having testified in court.

Former Liverpool and West Ham striker Carroll, who is now a player/co-owner of National League South club Dagenham & Redbridge, said the incident happened when he was sleeping. He said he then threw the man out of the house, and knocked him unconscious when he attempted to get back inside.

"I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now," wrote Carroll, who had decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing it with his girlfriend, Lou Teasdale.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

"Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

Carroll said testifying in court, where the attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register, was "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous."

The 37-year-old said: "What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including football ... The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

Prediction: The Dolphins were very impressive two weeks ago against the Warriors, restricting them to one try, before unleashing their signature attacking blitz after the break. Previously this season they have allowed teams to get away to big head starts before mounting their fightback, a ploy which just won't stand up in the finals. They appear to have taken note and their defensive work in New Zealand was outstanding. They will need to be at their very best once more against the Roosters, who have the attacking flair to cause them plenty of problems.

The Roosters were simply too good for the Sharks last week, after going very close to beating the Panthers the week before. They have plenty of experience across the park, with Daly Cherry-Evans putting in a much better performance against the Sharks in combination with the hard running Hugo Savala. Outside those two, the Roosters backline bristles with attacking weapons, with Robert Toia and Mark Nawaqanitawase in unstoppable form, James Tedesco always lurking, and Sam Walker returning at halfback.

But, as we all know, the backs don't win the big games, they just determine the score, and the Roosters have a pack that is the match of any in the league. Naufahu Whyte, Lindsay Collins and Siua Wong were at their destructive best against the Sharks. Add the menace of Victor Radley and Spencer Leniu, plus the returning Angus Crichton, and there isn't a weakness across the middle or on the edges.

The Dolphins will have to match the Roosters forwards, with Thomas Flegler, Tom Gilbert, Max Plath, Kulikefu Finefeuiaki, Ray Stone and Francis Molo all in for a big night. If they can negate the Roosters pack, we all know how devastating the Dolphins halves and backs can be.

Prediction: The best team of the 2026 season meets the hottest team of the 2026 finals in what should be another great game in front of a large crowd in Homebush.

The Panthers didn't have it all their way two weeks ago when defeating the Roosters, they were well-matched and needed a wobbly Nathan Cleary field goal to break a late deadlock. Cleary has been the focus ever since, as first he avoided suspension for a dangerous contact charge, and then set about rehabilitating an injured foot. The Panthers have proven they can win games without Cleary, but his coolness under pressure is invaluable in the biggest games.

The Knights are playing with the casino's money at this stage. After finishing last in 2025, making the finals surpassed anyone's expectations. To be playing in the Preliminary Final is an incredible achievement for coach Justin Holbrook and his team, especially considering they are without star half Dylan Brown. They simply have to keep playing the way they have been playing. Fast moving defence, free flowing ball movement from anywhere on the field, and total belief in their ability to beat anyone. Phoenix Crossland, Fletcher Sharpe, Kalyn Ponga, Bradman Best, Dan Gagai, Dom Young, the Knights have weapons across the field. Without Jacob Saifiti, they are a little light on up front, but veteran Tyson Frizell has stepped up in the middle and the Knights back-row ranks, strengthened now by the surprise return of Dylan Lucas, have been simply brilliant.

The big question is; can the Knights execute their attacking style against the best defence in the business? They played just the once this season, with the Panthers winning 44-12. We know how good the Panthers are. We have seen them dominate the big games for years. Cleary and Dylan Edwards orchestrating the attack, Isaah Yeo and Liam Martin leading the defence.
